samples.summary: New `POST tabs/:tabId/move` collides with (and shadows) the existing row/column axis-move route, breaking it
samples.evidence:
`ApiV1TabsController` is mounted at `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs` and the new handler is `@Post(':tabId/move')` (tabs.controller.ts:201) → path `.../documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId/move`.

`ApiV1WorksheetStructureController` is mounted at `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId` with `@Post('move')` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:256) → the *identical* path.

In `api-v1.module.ts` the controllers array lists `ApiV1TabsController` (line 56) before `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController` (line 64). Express/Nest dispatch to the first registered matching route, so every `POST .../tabs/<tab>/move` now lands in `ApiV1TabsController.move`, which requires `body.index` to be a positive integer and otherwise throws `BadRequestException`. The axis-move endpoint (`{ axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex }`) becomes unreachable and returns 400 for every request.

This is not hypothetical for callers: the CLI's own `moveAxis` posts to exactly the same URL — `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:978` `POST /documents/${docId}/tabs/${tabId}/move` — used by `sheets-structure.ts:224` (`sheets ... move` for rows/columns). So the new tab-move verb silently kills an existing, shipped row/column move capability (and the two CLI commands now target one endpoint with two incompatible bodies). One of the two paths must change (e.g. `tabs/:tabId/reorder` or `tabs/:tabId/move-tab`).

samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches anchors with `detachYorkieValue`, which mangles array-valued anchor fields (docs `posRange`, pdf-text `rects`) into CRDT metadata
samples.evidence:
`copyThread` does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {})` (comment-ops.ts:99), and the docblock claims "a recursive walk covers all three anchor shapes". But `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray` (yorkie-json.ts:172), and this very change documents that `Array.isArray` is **false** for a Yorkie array proxy — see the new docblock on `unwrapJson` (yorkie-json.ts:13-20) and the identical warning in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:62-70`: an array proxy "comes back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata". `comment-ops.ts` itself relies on that fact in `isThread` (line 125-130).

Two of the three anchor shapes the controller explicitly supports carry arrays:
- `docs-range.posRange` is a `TreePosStructRange`, i.e. a *pair* (array) of `TreePosStruct` (`packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31`).
- `pdf-text.rects` is an array of rectangles (`packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:57-63`, which copies it with `Array.from(...)` precisely because a spread/walk does not work).

So `GET /comments` (and the thread returned by reply/resolve) on a `doc` document, or on a PDF thread created from a text selection in the editor, returns `posRange` / `rects` as CRDT bookkeeping instead of positions — wrong data on a path the feature exists to serve (listing/replying to docs threads is the advertised capability, since creation is refused). The correct detach is the anchor's own `toJSON` via `unwrapJson`, or a field-wise copy like `copyAnchor`.

samples.summary: An unknown/typo `layoutId` silently produces a slide from the first built-in layout instead of failing
samples.evidence: `addSlide(document, layoutId, position)` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, which resolves it via `resolveLayout` → `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-178), and `getLayout` is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(l => l.id === layoutId) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198). There is no `not_found` result for a bad layout id, so `POST .../slides` with `layoutId: 'two-contnet'` returns 200 and inserts a slide built from an entirely different layout. The endpoint's stated purpose is to make `layoutId` usable (`listLayouts` exists for that), so silently substituting a layout is a wrong result for ordinary input; it should be validated against the deck's layouts ∪ built-ins and 400/404 otherwise.

samples.summary: Image `anchor` validation via `parseRef` accepts malformed A1 refs (lowercase, non-letter column, row 0), storing an unplaceable anchor
samples.evidence: `parseImage` validates the anchor only by `parseRef(anchor)` not throwing (worksheet-images.ts:44-49). `parseRef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:323-354) does no character-class check: it finds the first digit and reduces the preceding characters with `char.charCodeAt(0) - 65 + 1`. So `"a1"` → column 33, `"!1"` → column -31, `"A0"` → row 0 — none throw, all are accepted and written into `ws.images[id].anchor`. The comments controller is protected from this by a second check (`rowOrder?.[r-1]`/`colOrder?.[c-1]` must exist, comments.controller.ts:653-660), but the image writer has no such check, so a malformed anchor is persisted and the renderer positions the picture off-grid. A regex such as `/^\$?[A-Z]+\$?[1-9]\d*$/` (or `parseARef`, which does match a strict pattern) is what this needs.

samples.summary: `deleteThread` 404s "Comment not found" for a thread whose comment list is empty, instead of deleting it
samples.evidence: The authorize callback calls `this.assertCommentAuthor(map, threadId, rootCommentId(thread), author)`; `rootCommentId` returns `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id` — `undefined` when the stored thread has no comments (comments.controller.ts:613-615). `assertCommentAuthor` then takes the `commentId ? ... : undefined` branch and throws `NotFoundException('Comment not found')` (line 527-528). A degenerate/legacy thread with an empty `comments` array therefore becomes undeletable through the API and reports a misleading 404 about a comment, even though the thread it names does exist.

samples.summary: `applySlideChange` move-to-front falls through to `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` when the array exposes `moveAfterByIndex` but not `moveFront`
samples.evidence: The branch is `if (slides.moveAfterByIndex && slides.getElementByIndex) { if (to === 0 && slides.moveFront) {...} else if (to > from) {...} else { slides.moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from); } }`. With `to === 0` and `moveFront` absent (all three reorder methods are optional on `SlideArrayLike`), the final branch calls `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` — a negative predecessor index. Unreachable with the real Yorkie proxy (which has all three) and with a plain array (which has none), but the guard as written admits a partial-capability object into a nonsense call; guarding the whole in-place path on `moveFront` too would close it.

verdict.reason: Verified every claim directly. tabs.controller.ts:33 mounts at `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs` and tabs.controller.ts:201 declares `@Post(':tabId/move')`, producing `.../tabs/:tabId/move`. worksheet-structure.controller.ts:62 mounts at `.../tabs/:tabId` and worksheet-structure.controller.ts:256 declares `@Post('move')`, producing the identical path. Both controllers are in the same `controllers` array in api-v1.module.ts, with ApiV1TabsController at line 56 ahead of ApiV1WorksheetStructureController at line 64, so Nest/Express dispatches every POST to that path into the tab handler. That handler rejects at tabs.controller.ts:211-215 with BadRequestException unless `body.index` is an integer >= 1, while the axis endpoint's payload is `{axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex}` (parsed at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:264) and carries no `index` — so axis moves return 400 unconditionally and the axis handler is unreachable. The path is exercised by shipped callers: http-client.ts:975-978 `moveAxis` POSTs `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tabId}/move` from sheets-structure.ts:224, and http-client.ts:542-545 `moveTab` posts the same URL from tabs.ts:165. I searched for @Version/host route scoping in packages/backend/src/api/v1 and found none, so nothing disambiguates the two routes. worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts contains no createNestApplication/supertest/request(app), meaning it calls the controller method directly and cannot detect the routing shadow — so passing tests are not a guard. No refutation ground applies: code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and a wrong-handler dispatch breaking a shipped endpoint is squarely correctness (broken invariant / core flow broken), justifying critical severity.

mergedFrom.summary: `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so `listThreads`/`findThread` reject every thread actually stored in the CRDT

finding.summary: `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` guard is false for every real Yorkie thread, so `listThreads`/`findThread` skip all stored threads — the whole comments API reads empty and every reply/resolve/delete 404s
finding.evidence: `listThreads` (line 116) and `findThread` (line 129) both bail with `!Array.isArray(thread.comments)`. This repo documents the opposite of the assumption in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:67-70`: "`detachYorkieValue` does not save it either — it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for an array proxy". Inside `withDocument`, `map[threadId].comments` is a Yorkie array proxy, so both guards evaluate to `continue`/`undefined` for genuine threads. Consequences: `GET .../comments` returns `{threads: []}`; `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:709-713) never finds a tab, so `mutateMap` throws `NotFoundException`; the flat doc/pdf path's `findThread(doc.getRoot().comments, threadId)` (comments.controller.ts:463) also 404s. Every reply, resolve, unresolve, thread delete and comment delete therefore fails against a real document. Note the same file uses `Array.from(t.comments ?? [])` at line 99 (the proxy-safe form the frontend uses) — the guard is inconsistent with it. The unit tests cannot catch this because `comment-ops.spec.ts` and `comments.controller.spec.ts` both build threads as plain JS objects.

verdict.reason: The alleged `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` guard is not in the code. `comment-ops.ts:125-130` (`isThread`) tests array-likeness — `typeof comments.length === 'number'` after an object check — which is true for both a Yorkie array proxy and a plain array. The only `Array.isArray` text in the file is the doc comment at lines 112-113 explicitly warning against that exact trap. `listThreads` (line 138) and `findThread` (line 149) both delegate to `isThread`, so the claimed cascade (empty `GET .../comments`, `tabIdOfThread` at comments.controller.ts:723 failing, flat-doc `findThread` at comments.controller.ts:461 404ing) does not follow. A repo-wide grep for `Array.isArray` in packages/backend/src finds no such guard on any comments path (the two hits in comments.controller.ts:618,677 are request-body/rect JSON validation). The claim that tests cannot catch it is also false: comment-ops.spec.ts:92-121 exercises a Proxy for which `Array.isArray` is asserted false (line 114) and asserts findThread/listThreads still resolve it. The finding describes a prior state, not the working tree.

finding.summary: `applySetResolved` unconditionally `delete`s `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` on reopen; deleting a key that is not present on a Yorkie object throws, so `PATCH {resolved:false}` on a never-resolved thread can 500
finding.evidence: comment-ops.ts:214-224 runs `delete thread.resolvedAt` / `delete thread.resolvedBy` whenever `resolved === false`, with no existence check. Yorkie's object proxy `deleteProperty` routes to `CRDTObject.deleteByKey` → `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which raises `fail to find <key>` when the key was never set. The route accepts `{resolved:false}` on any thread (comments.controller.ts:368-379), including one that was never resolved or one reopened twice — cases the editor UI cannot produce (its reopen control only exists on resolved threads), which is why the identical frontend code at yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:142-143 never hits it. Result: a 500 on an idempotent reopen.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `applySetResolved` (comment-ops.ts:285-308) does not unconditionally delete `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` on reopen: each delete sits in an `else if (thread.resolvedAt !== undefined)` / `else if (thread.resolvedBy !== undefined)` existence guard (lines 298-302 and 303-307), so a never-resolved thread reaches neither `delete`. The reviewer's cited range comment-ops.ts:214-224 holds `findComment`/`commentAuthorId` and contains no `delete` at all. The rationale for the guard — Yorkie's `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey` throwing `fail to find <key>`, and `PATCH {resolved:false}` being accepted on any thread — is documented at comment-ops.ts:279-283, and a regression test at comment-ops.spec.ts:153-172 wraps the thread in a Proxy whose `deleteProperty` throws for absent keys and asserts `applySetResolved(strict, false, ...)` does not throw with zero deletes attempted. The only production call site, comments.controller.ts:395 (from `PATCH :threadId`, lines 376-404), routes through this guarded function, and a repo-wide grep for `delete thread.resolved` finds no unguarded backend duplicate. The idempotent-reopen 500 the finding predicts cannot occur.
